Question Choices: A fair die is rolled once and 'success' means rolling a 6. What is q, the probability of failure?
In Lotto 6-49 you must correctly guess 6 different numbers from 1 to 49. How many equally likely 6-number combinations are there? (This is the denominator of p.)
Hints: Order does not matter, so count combinations;Compute C(49,6)=49!/(6!·43!)
Solution: The number of combinations is $\binom{49}{6}=\frac{49\cdot48\cdot47\cdot46\cdot45\cdot44}{6!}=13983816$.;So the probability of winning one Bernoulli trial is $p=\frac{1}{13983816}$.

Question Choices: Which of the following is NOT a Bernoulli trial? Choices: A) Flipping a coin and recording heads or tails | B) Taking a test and recording pass or fail | C) Rolling a die and recording the number shown | D) Drawing an item and recording whether it is defective Answer with the letter only.
Hints: A Bernoulli trial has exactly two outcomes
Solution: Rolling a die and recording the number has six outcomes, not two, so it is not a Bernoulli trial. The answer is C.
